taxonomyNote: NatureServe lists the synonym S. obesus and notes Sumarli et al. (2024) suggest most Baja California peninsula populations may be a different species.
fieldMarks: Large, flattened, dark-bodied lizard with loose skin folds on the neck and sides, small granular scales, and a blunt, broad-based tail.
Adult males mainly dark (marked gray, red or yellow) with a pale yellow tail; females retain juvenile crossbands.
Young are crossbanded brown and gray-brown on body and tail.
Largest native iguanid in the US: adult snout-vent length usually 14-20 cm; lacks head horns and expanded toe tips.
behavior: Basks on rocks by day; inactive in cold or extreme heat, but can be active most of the year in mild winters.
Herbivore: browses leaves, buds, flowers and fruit; occasionally insects.
Retreats into rock crevices, puffing up with air to wedge in (BLM Red Rock Canyon leaflet).
Lays 5-16 eggs underground, about June-August; life expectancy about 15 years.
habitat: Rocky desert: lava flows, hillsides and outcrops, typically with creosote bush.
range: Southern Nevada, southern Utah, southeastern California and western Arizona south to southern Baja California and west-central Sonora, Mexico.

lookalikes.name: Gila monster
lookalikes.howToTell: Dorsal scales are large and beadlike and lack femoral pores; chuckwalla has small granular scales and femoral pores.
